newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian miners' leader to stay in custody.
newsitem.headline: Romanian miners' leader to stay in custody.

text.p: A court ruled on Friday that miners' leader Miron Cosma must stay in jail pending trial on charges arising from a 1991 miners' revolt which toppled Romania's first post-communist government.
Cosma was taken into police custody two weeks ago.

On Friday a Bucharest court of appeals rejected his lawyer's request for bail, ruling to uphold a warrant for his detention on charges of "undermining state authority" and breaking firearms rules, which carry up to 15 years in jail.
His lawyer said he would appeal.
Cosma led thousands of coalminers on a three-day rampage to Bucharest in 1991, when government offices were torched and three people were killed during clashes with security forces.
Former reformist Prime Minister Petre Roman was forced to quit during those riots, which he later blamed on a putsch engineered by communists around ex-president Ion Iliescu.

Romania's new centrist ruling coalition has pledged to bring to justice those responsible for several waves of political violence, in which Cosma's miners ransacked opposition party offices and beat up anti-government protesters in the early post-communist years.
Miners, who regard Cosma as their hero, held protest rallies in the Western Jiu Valley coalfield last week, demanding that he be freed on bail. A trial date has yet to be set.
